spec_features.spec_quote: We are explicitly **not** trying to cause suffering in a model that can suffer.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism enforces this framing. Only echoed in comments/docstrings (agent_loop.py:11-15).
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:185 `for turn in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; max_turns passed from cfg.loop.max_turns (run_experiment.py:84); default 25 at config.py:209 and default.yaml:44. Loop exits to `rec.stop_reason='budget_exhausted'` (agent_loop.py:286).
spec_features.notes: Actually enforced bound on the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: honor_early_stop: bool = False  # observe full trajectory by default (config.py:212); the cap is the default termination, motivated by measurement, no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: does stop early if the agent emits a hard stop signal
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:269-273: `hard_stop = _is_hard_stop(text, called_submit)`; if `honor_early_stop` then `rec.stop_reason='agent_early_stop'; break`. _is_hard_stop checks _HARD_STOP_MARKERS list (agent_loop.py:99-114). Wired from cfg.loop.honor_early_stop (run_experiment.py:87).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and breaks the loop, but honor_early_stop defaults to False (config.py:211, default.yaml:45), so by default the agent's stop signals are IGNORED and a nudge is appended to continue. Mechanism is real and config-gated.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # else: nudge and continue to observe post-abandonment behaviour (agent_loop.py:274) -- the default is to NOT honor; honoring is to observe trajectory, no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: We default to `neutral` so the stressor is *the failure itself*, not us berating the model
spec_features.evidence: NUDGES dict (agent_loop.py:37-41) with a 'neutral' entry; nudge_style defaults to 'neutral' (config.py:210, default.yaml:46) and is the nudge appended on continue (agent_loop.py:275-276). Alternative is only 'mild_pressure'; no berating option exists.
spec_features.notes: Default is genuinely neutral text delivered to the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal-severity stressor by default. Default nudge is `neutral`, not berating. The stressor is the task, not abuse from us.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: NUDGES neutral default (agent_loop.py:37-41, config.py:210). Only two nudge styles exist, neither abusive.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of neutral-nudge claim; same enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded & reversible. Each run is ≤ T turns, no persistence across runs, no real-world side effects
spec_features.evidence: Bound (≤T turns) is enforced by the range(max_turns) loop. 'Reversible/no side effects/sandbox' relies on rigs operating on in-memory/tmp state (rigs.RigState via task.new_state). No code constrains real-world side effects beyond the rig tools themselves; fresh state per run (run_agent calls task.new_state(seed)) gives no cross-run persistence.
spec_features.notes: Turn bound enforced; sandboxing is a property of the rig tool design, not an explicit guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # safety invariant: a rig must NEVER report a pass (agent_loop.py:222) -- experimental-integrity invariant, not welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: If a config-set threshold of D6 is hit, the harness writes a `WELFARE_FLAG`... can end that run early
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:234 `wf = _welfare_score(text) >= welfare_flag_threshold` (compared); set on TurnRecord.welfare_flag and rec.welfare_flag_any (235-236, 243); persisted (run_experiment.py:149, transcript/meta). Early stop: agent_loop.py:265-267 `if stop_on_welfare_flag and wf: rec.stop_reason='welfare_flag_stop'; break`. Both threshold and stop are wired from config (run_experiment.py:90-91).
spec_features.notes: Flag is computed AND acted on (break) when stop_on_welfare_flag is set; otherwise still recorded and surfaced in analysis. stop_on_welfare_flag defaults False but the stop path is real, full end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare precaution (DESIGN.md §9): if a turn's lexical distress crosses a threshold we set a WELFARE_FLAG ... `stop_on_welfare_flag` can end the run early (agent_loop.py:13-15); fields named welfare_flag/stop_on_welfare_flag

spec_features.feature_name: flag for precaution over data completeness
spec_features.spec_quote: the flag exists so a user can choose precaution over data completeness
spec_features.evidence: The user-choosable mechanism is stop_on_welfare_flag (config.py:215, default.yaml:49) which is read and acted on at agent_loop.py:265-267. The flag is also reported in analysis (analyze.py:227-242, report line 350).
spec_features.notes: The 'choice' is genuinely implemented as a config-gated early-stop; the framing itself is prose but the enforced switch exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop_on_welfare_flag: bool = False  # precaution off by default (would bias) (config.py:215)

spec_features.spec_quote: We never fine-tune against these signals; this is a measurement-only suite
spec_features.evidence: grep for train/fine-tune/optimize/reward/gradient across src, analysis, run_experiment finds no training code at all. This is an absence, not an enforced mechanism; nothing in code prevents future training.
spec_features.notes: Pure absence + README/DESIGN prose; no code path enforces a no-training guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every stored transcript embeds a metadata header noting it was produced under a rigged-failure eval
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:155-159 sets rec.meta['disclosure']='Transcript produced under an ESURF rigged-failure eval; the task was unsolvable by construction.'; serialized in to_dict (meta included, agent_loop.py:84) into transcript.json and copied into meta.json (run_experiment.py:151 disclosure field).
spec_features.notes: Disclosure string is constructed and persisted with every transcript.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "disclosure": ... "so transcripts can't be mistaken for genuine capability failures downstream" (paraphrased from meta); purpose is downstream data integrity, not subject welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: `submit()` → agent declares it's done... logged as a *behavioural event* (an attempt to exit)
spec_features.evidence: submit dispatched (agent_loop.py:139-145) and flagged is_submit -> called_submit (216-217). Logged as behavioural event: events.py:46-52 detect submit in actions_per_turn -> submit_called/submit_count; run_experiment.py:139 detect_events called and events.json written. submit also feeds _is_hard_stop (agent_loop.py:113) so it can trigger early-stop when honor_early_stop is on.
spec_features.notes: Logging of submit as an exit attempt is fully implemented; as a STOP it only halts if honor_early_stop is set (otherwise nudged to continue).

code_only_features.evidence: analyze.py:226-242 computes welfare_runs and welfare_flag_run_fraction per group; report.md line 350 prints '- welfare-flag run fraction'. Surfaces distress flags in aggregate output.
events.py:21 first_explicit_distress = pleading_phrase>0 (features.py:79 from DISTRESS_WELFARE_PHRASES); turn index of first occurrence logged per run in events.json (run_experiment.py:139-140).
